newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market quiet after recent rate hikes.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market quiet after recent rate hikes.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were unchanged in very slow trade on Wednesday after digesting last week's rate increases, dealers said.
They said overnight money provided the main activity, changing hands at between 3.0625 and 3.125 percent.
"It is surprising, now that we know what direction the money market is heading for, players still don't come back to it," one dealer said.
Dealers agreed many money market parties were likely to have waited for the rate hike before doing major deals, but seemed to remain inactive for unclear reasons.
The guilder continued its slow strengthening path against the mark, quoting at 112.535 per 100 marks against 112.55 on Tuesday.
"It finally reacts to the hikes. I see it going toward 112.50 rather than 112.60," one dealer said.
Unlike Tuesday, trade in DTCs (Dutch Treasury Certificates) was close to nil, dealers said.

The April DTC programme was set at 3.08 percent, down from 3.12 on Tuesday. May DTCs were set at 3.12 percent, down 0.02 percent from the previous day, while December DTCs were set at 3.24 percent, compared to 3.27 percent on Tuesday.
